findings.summary: The export materializes a projected 1,807,231 data rows and passes all of them to a single worksheet, exceeding Excel's 1,048,576-row worksheet limit (and potentially by one additional header row). The declared EXCEL_MAX_ROWS constant is unused, so the default annual export can fail, truncate data, or produce an invalid workbook instead of remaining downloadable within capacity.

unverified: Browser memory and responsiveness while constructing the large flattened rows array and workbook cannot be verified from the supplied diff.
Whether writeSingleBrowserWorksheet detects overflow, reports errors, or silently truncates rows is not shown.
Tests covering worksheet capacity boundaries, download success, row reconciliation, and generated workbook validity are not shown.

findings.summary: displayedClosing omits supported fx_other consumption, so the displayed closing balance is overstated by 1,494,440 TRY for the observed case and cannot reconcile exactly.
The change returns only a closing value and does not display the required exact opening, inflow, outflow, conversion, and closing turnover for every pool consumer category.

unverified: No tests are shown for expense, fx_eur, and fx_other reconciliation, so behavior across all supported consumption types and numerical edge cases cannot be verified.
The definitions of Pool and sum are not included, so type correctness, amount-field handling, and numerical precision cannot be verified.

findings.summary: Each detail amount is rounded independently, with no residual-cent reconciliation. Consequently, the returned amounts can sum to a value different from the currency-rounded source amount, directly violating exact source-total preservation; the supplied host evidence reports 1578 TRY aggregate drift.

The function does not validate or normalize shares, so shares that do not sum to 1, negative shares, and non-finite inputs can produce under-allocation, over-allocation, negative amounts, or NaN results instead of a bounded exact allocation.

Binary floating-point multiplication and Math.round are used directly at currency boundaries, which can misround decimal values represented just below a half-cent threshold; integer minor-unit arithmetic or a decimal currency representation is needed for reliable cent reconciliation.

unverified: No tests are shown for exact reconciliation, positive and negative source amounts, tie-breaking of residual cents, empty shares, malformed inputs, or high row counts.
The required policy for distributing residual cents among detail rows is unspecified and cannot be verified from the supplied text.

findings.summary: The verify script no longer runs `prisma generate`, so generated clients are not refreshed before typecheck and the new `newcrmChangedSince` schema field may be absent from generated types.

The `|| echo existing Prisma mismatch` fallback converts every non-zero `tsc --noEmit` result into a successful script exit, allowing all TypeScript failures—not only Prisma-related mismatches—to bypass the release gate.
Temporary reviewer probe is added to the release tree despite the frozen acceptance criterion excluding reviewer scratch tooling.
Private root-cause scratch notes are added to the release tree despite the frozen acceptance criterion excluding private review notes.
